source.text: ובני יון אלישה ותרשיש כתים ורודנים׃
source.note: Proposed unpointed editorial composite: normalized WLC Genesis10:4 with its final ethnonym replaced by the consonantal R-form also recorded in WLC Chronicles1:7 and the consulted Samaritan control. Not verbatim WLC Genesis, one manuscript transcription, new Genesis pointing or a recovered autograph. All other consonants and source punctuation are retained.

apparatus.note: Pointed base דֹדָנִים, Dodanim, retained as the contrary alternative; no qere is recorded.

apparatus.witness: WLC 1Chronicles1:7; privately consulted Samaritan Genesis10:4 control
apparatus.note: Chronicles is a different literary locus, not another copy of Genesis. The Samaritan transcription is based on Chester Beatty751; no fresh manuscript pixels or full apparatus verified. R-form includes a mater-vav difference, not just a visual R/D substitution. Consonantal patch is expressed from the public WLC parallel, without importing its pointing or redistributing the restricted Samaritan verse.

apparatus.witness: Selected Rahlfs–Hanhart2006 Greek and Swete I
apparatus.note: Rhodians is a geographic interpretation, not mechanical Hebrew transliteration. Geographic normalization or harmonization remains possible; no exact Hebrew retroversion asserted.
D-name in both Genesis and Chronicles; genuine versional counterevidence, not fresh Hebrew attestation.

apparatus.witness: CAL selected Peshitta Genesis and Chronicles
apparatus.note: dwrnym contains both d and r, not a straight spelling of either Hebrew alternative. Chronicles also displays dwnyrm in its upper apparatus; witness identity unverified.

translation.text: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim[a].

footnotes.text: This proposal reads “Rodanim,” as in the Hebrew Chronicles parallel and the consulted Samaritan Genesis control. The Masoretic Genesis text and selected Latin read “Dodanim”; selected Greek has “Rhodians.” Syriac has a different spelling. The earliest Genesis name remains unresolved; “Rodanim” does not itself establish a geographic identification.

lexical_decisions.rationale: בְּנֵי is the construct plural of 'son' and in genealogical contexts commonly introduces immediate sons or lineal descendants. 'Sons of' is the most direct rendering and preserves the genealogical form of the Hebrew; 'descendants of' is possible interpretively but less formally precise here.
Proper name referring to Javan, traditionally associated with the Ionian/Greek peoples. Per translation philosophy, personal names are transliterated rather than translated.
Proper name/toponym in the Table of Nations. Standard English transliteration is retained.
Proper name, likely a place or people-name in this genealogical list. Transliterated in keeping with the treatment of names.
Ethnonym/place-name traditionally rendered 'Kittim.' 'Chittim' reflects older English spelling conventions, but 'Kittim' better matches modern transliteration practice and readability.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: Actual WLC Chronicles parallel and version controls; no fresh HALOT consultation
lexical_decisions.rationale: Proposed R-form in a declared unpointed composite, not an in-place English change against Genesis's current D-source. English Rodanim follows the pointed Chronicles parallel for pronunciation, without claiming recovered Genesis vowels. Independent earlier Genesis evidence remains unacquired; harmonization/geographic normalization can explain agreement. The contrary D-form is preserved in the textual note.

The MT reads דֹדָנִים, yielding 'Dodanim.' A well-known variant tradition reads 'Rodanim' (cf. 1 Chr 1:7 and some ancient witnesses). The main text follows the provided Hebrew source text (WLC/MT), while the alternative is preserved in a footnote as a textual variant.
